about.title: About
body: Backend-focused Full Stack Java Developer and Computer Science graduate. In 2026 I built features for the Government Savings Bank (GSB) Corporate Internet Banking platform using Java and Spring MVC, working across both the corporate-customer and bank-officer sides of the system.

Before that, during my internship, I built and shipped a Pre/Post Anesthetic electronic medical record system end to end — now in real use by the anesthesiology department at Phrapokklao Hospital, replacing paper-based records.
I care about writing clean, reliable code that holds up in production, and I'm currently looking for a Java / Backend or Full Stack Developer role.

items.context: Corporate Internet Banking (CIB), Government Savings Bank — via MFEC (System Integrator)
bullets: Enhanced the maker–approver workflow: maker-selectable approver routing across all financial services, and authorizer roll-over of future-dated (scheduled) transactions using the Quartz scheduler.
Delivered a transaction-cancellation feature to void any service type that is pending approval, or approved but not yet processed.
On the bank-officer admin front, built range-based approval-limit configuration and a registration flow supporting single-user (sole-proprietor) accounts.
Wrote and optimized SQL and managed relational data on IBM Db2 via DBeaver.
Deployed WAR builds to JBoss/Tomcat and troubleshot production issues via MobaXterm with Log4j2 log analysis.
Collaborated through GitHub code reviews in a 7-person Agile team, and contributed to requirement analysis, testing and maintenance.
items.stack: Java · Spring MVC · JDBC · IBM Db2 · JSP · Quartz · GitHub · Eclipse IDE · DBeaver · MobaXterm

items.context: Pre/Post Anesthetic electronic medical record (eMR) system
bullets: Built and deployed a web system replacing paper-based pre- and post-anesthetic assessment records with structured electronic forms — now in real use by the anesthesiology department.

Integrated the application with the hospital information system (HIS) across seven REST endpoints through a server-side proxy that attached authentication and kept upstream endpoints out of the browser.
Implemented JWT authentication over HttpOnly cookies with an administrator approval workflow for new accounts and role-based access control.
Designed a MySQL schema storing each record in two layers — raw JSON for re-editing and rendered text for printing and submission.
Containerized the stack with Docker Compose for reproducible deployment.
items.stack: PHP 8 · JavaScript · Tailwind CSS · Bootstrap · MySQL 8 · REST API · JWT · Docker Compose

items.name: GSB Corporate Internet Banking
items.context: A live Corporate Internet Banking platform for a national bank, where every financial transaction passes through a maker–approver flow with per-service approval rules. I worked change requests across both the corporate-customer front (CF) and the bank-officer admin front (BF), inside a Java / Spring MVC codebase that had been in production for years.
items.decision: Every change had to extend the existing approval and status model rather than replace it — the platform is live and each service type has its own transaction lifecycle. I kept the work inside the established Controller–Service–DAO layering and reused the existing status codes, so new behaviour composes with rules already running in production instead of being special-cased.
items.outcome: Each change request went through the bank's UAT cycle, with defects tracked and re-tested across both the Thai and English UI and every affected service type.
highlights: Maker–approver routing across fund transfer, bulk transfer, bill payment, direct credit, EWHT and BahtNet
Roll-over of future-dated transactions within the effective-date window (Quartz scheduler)
Transaction cancellation before the processing cutoff, across all service types
Range-based approval limits and a registration flow for sole-proprietor accounts

items.name: Anest — Pre/Post Anesthetic eMR
items.context: The anesthesiology department at Phrapokklao Hospital recorded pre- and post-anesthetic assessments on paper. The replacement had to be editable by clinicians, printable, and ultimately submitted back into the hospital information system (HIS). Built end to end during my internship.
items.decision: Two decisions shaped the design. The browser never talks to hospital APIs directly — a server-side proxy attaches credentials and whitelists query parameters, so upstream endpoints and tokens are never exposed to the client. And each record is stored twice: raw JSON so a clinician can reopen and edit the form, plus rendered text for printing and HIS submission — trading a little storage for the ability to change the form layout without breaking historical records.
items.outcome: In real use by the department, replacing paper records. Ships as a Docker Compose stack (PHP/Apache + MySQL 8 + phpMyAdmin) so it can be brought up reproducibly; a sanitised demo build with mock data is open source.
highlights: JWT authentication over HttpOnly cookies with role-based access and admin approval of new accounts
Secure server-side REST proxy integrating hospital HIS data across seven endpoints
MySQL schema storing each record as raw JSON plus print-ready text
Dockerized with Docker Compose — one command to run the whole stack
items.imageAlt: Anest eMR dashboard showing the patient record list (demo data)

items.name: Ledger API — double-entry accounting service
items.context: Working on a banking platform taught me that the hard part of moving money is not the write itself — it is what happens when the same write arrives twice, when two requests race, and when a wrong entry has to be corrected without erasing history. I built this in C# and ASP.NET Core to tackle those problems directly, and to move into .NET properly rather than by tutorial.
items.decision: Balances are never stored. An account has no balance column; a balance is summed from its journal lines, which removes the lost-update race by construction rather than guarding against it. Idempotency is likewise pushed down to the database: a reservation row keyed on (endpoint, Idempotency-Key) means PostgreSQL decides which of two simultaneous retries proceeds — a check-then-insert in application code would still lose that race. Corrections are reversing entries, never updates or deletes, so history stays replayable for an auditor.
items.outcome: 52 tests, green in CI. The integration suite runs against a real PostgreSQL container rather than an in-memory provider, because the guarantee depends on an actual unique-constraint violation. It was that suite that caught a bug where the request fingerprint was silently hashing an empty stream — the protection looked like it worked and did nothing.
highlights: Eight simultaneous retries with one Idempotency-Key create exactly one entry — asserted, not assumed
Debits must equal credits; decimal and numeric(19,4) end to end, never floating point
Reversal instead of update or delete, with both entries pointing at each other
Trial balance nets to zero after randomised postings — one assertion that catches almost any posting bug
CI fails the build on a dependency with a published CVE, not just on a failing test
items.imageAlt: Diagram: two simultaneous retries with the same Idempotency-Key result in exactly one journal entry
